items.followUp: Derive the equation for the gravitational potential energy gained by an object raised through a height h.

rubric.description: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining kinetic energy as energy due to motion.

rubric.why: Relates the work done to the force and acceleration.
rubric.description: The work done is W = Fs, and the force is F = ma.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both relations are stated.

rubric.why: Uses the equation of motion for a body starting from rest to find its displacement.
rubric.description: For a body starting from rest, v² = u² + 2as and u = 0, so s = v²/(2a).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the motion equation, initial condition, and resulting displacement.

rubric.why: Substitutes the displacement into the work expression and states the kinetic-energy equation.
rubric.description: W = mas = ½mv²; therefore, KE = ½mv².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for deriving or stating the final equation.

modelAnswer: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
The work done to bring a body from rest to speed v is its kinetic energy.
W = Fs and F = ma, so W = mas.
For a body starting from rest, v² = u² + 2as and u = 0; therefore, s = v²/(2a).

items.followUp: Explain why the pressure exerted by a liquid increases with depth, using the equation for pressure in a liquid.

rubric.why: Relates the liquid column's volume to its cross-sectional area and depth.
rubric.description: For a liquid column of area A and depth h, its volume is V = Ah.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the volume relation.

rubric.why: Uses the definition of density to express the liquid's mass.
rubric.description: The mass of the liquid is m = rho V = rho Ah.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for expressing mass in terms of density and volume or area and depth.

rubric.why: Expresses the force exerted by the liquid column as its weight.
rubric.description: The column's weight is F = mg = rho Ahg.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the weight relation or its expression using density, area, and depth.

rubric.why: Divides the force by area and obtains the pressure at depth h.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the final pressure equation.

modelAnswer: Consider a liquid column of depth h and cross-sectional area A.
The volume of the column is V = Ah.
If the liquid density is rho, its mass is m = rho V = rho Ah.
The weight of the liquid column is F = mg = rho Ahg.
Pressure at the depth is P = F/A = rho Ahg/A.
